title: Expose optimization config version pinning via Helm values + document rollback procedure
author: Bruno Silva
body: Summary: This PR adds first-class Helm values to pin the active Optimization Config version for Redwood Private installs and documents an operator-friendly rollback flow (pin to prior version + apply). Motivation: In Hosted/Dedicated, the control plane manages versioning and rollback; for Private, operators need a deterministic way to (a) hold a known-good version during upgrades and (b) roll back quickly when an optimization change causes a latency/5xx regression. This change introduces an explicit chart-level mechanism to pass the pinned version to the control plane/runtime, making the procedure consistent with the Safe Apply + Rollback project. What’s included: (1) New values: optimize.optimizationConfig.versionPin (string, optional) and optimize.optimizationConfig.allowUnpinned (bool, default true). When versionPin is set, the deployment will request that version from the Optimization Config Service and treat it as the active version for the configured scope. (2) Templating: inject OPTIMIZATION_CONFIG_VERSION_PIN and OPTIMIZATION_CONFIG_ALLOW_UNPINNED into the control-plane and runtime components; add checksum annotations so updating values triggers rollouts. (3) Validation: fail chart rendering when versionPin is set but empty/whitespace; add a warning note in NOTES.txt when allowUnpinned=false and no pin is supplied. (4) Docs: add a dedicated “Rollback optimization config” section with a copy-paste example (helm upgrade --set optimize.optimizationConfig.versionPin=<prior_version>) and post-rollback verification steps (check rollout status, confirm config_version tag on metrics, confirm p95 recovery). Backwards compatibility: Existing installs that do not set versionPin behave as before (control plane uses the currently-promoted version / unpinned resolution). No changes to defaults that would impact current clusters. Testing: helm lint, helm template, and a minimal kind-based smoke deploy in CI to ensure env vars are present and rollouts happen on pin changes. Follow-ups: (a) In a separate PR we can add a small “pin status” panel to the Private operator docs to align with Console wording, (b) add a values.schema.json pattern restriction once we finalize the canonical version ID format (currently treated as opaque string).
commits: templates: wire version pin env vars into control-plane + runtime deployments
templates: add checksum annotation for optimization config pin changes
docs: document rollback procedure and verification checklist
ci: add helm template assertions for optimization config env vars
review_conversation: Vivek Kulkarni: Can we make sure updating versionPin forces a rollout? We’ve been burned by config-only changes not triggering new pods. Bruno Silva: Added checksum annotation keyed off the rendered env var values; confirmed that helm upgrade changes ReplicaSet hash. Ethan Park: Naming question—can we avoid calling it “activeVersion” since runtime semantics treat it as a pin override rather than a promotion? Bruno Silva: Renamed to optimize.optimizationConfig.versionPin and updated docs to call it “pin”; promotion remains a control-plane concept. Kira Thompson: The rollback docs should include a clear verification checklist and mention where to look for the applied version. Bruno Silva: Added steps: kubectl describe pod env var, check metrics tag config_version, and validate p95/5xx stabilization window. Connor O'Brien: CI failed on the first run due to values.schema.json indentation; please rerun once fixed. Bruno Silva: Fixed schema formatting, re-ran CI, all green. Approvals: Vivek Kulkarni approved; Ethan Park approved; Kira Thompson approved; Connor O’Brien approved with note to reference GA checklist doc in follow-up.
release_notes: Private (Helm): Operators can pin an Optimization Config version via values to support safe rollback and deterministic behavior during upgrades.
Docs: Added rollback procedure and verification checklist for optimization config changes.
